strengths: Novel conceptual contribution: The 'shadow' metaphor and latent space construction provides genuine insight into zonotope propagation, offering an elegant reframing of known techniques
Sound mathematical foundation: Proposition 2 is correctly developed and enables practical backward constraint propagation; proofs are valid
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Fair comparison with top-5 VNN-COMP'24 tools, extensive ablations, diverse benchmarks, and clear documentation of setup
Practical GPU acceleration: Focus on matrix-only operations yields meaningful speedups (37.5s → 1.9s with batch size 1024); implementation is efficient
Clear presentation: Well-written paper with effective visualizations (Figures 1-3) that build strong intuition for key concepts
weaknesses: Empirical results are competitive but not dominant: Performance gaps vs. leading tools on several benchmarks (e.g., 80% vs 87.8% on cora); matches top performance on only 3 of 7 benchmarks, weakening claims of strong practical impact

Limited technical novelty: Core techniques (iterative refinement, constrained zonotopes, dependency extraction) are largely from prior work [24,33,37,38]; novelty is primarily in conceptual integration rather than algorithmic advances

Insufficient algorithmic justification: Set-based falsification (Sec 4.2) lacks depth—no analysis of why boundary points outperform FGSM; splitting heuristic unablated; layer-wise vs network-wise differences marginal

Narrow scope and generalization concerns: Approach specific to zonotopes + ReLU networks; limited discussion of extension to other set representations (star sets, polynomial zonotopes) or activation functions

Incomplete evaluation: No direct runtime comparison on identical hardware; counterexample extraction barely evaluated (1 metric on 1 benchmark); missing ablation isolating latent space insight contribution
Reproducibility limitations: MATLAB implementation not standard for performance-critical tools; code availability not mentioned; approximation quality impact (Prop. 3) not analyzed

Overclaimed results: 'Significantly reduce' subproblems but Table 2a shows modest improvements (406.9→406.1 for network-wise refinement); claims of 'top-ranking placement' not fully supported by mixed benchmark results

strengths: Clear and elegant latent space insight with formal mathematical grounding (Proposition 2 with soundness proof in Corollary 1)
Comprehensive evaluation on standardized VNN-COMP'24 benchmarks against top-5 tools with competitive results (matching top performance on 4/8 benchmarks)
Extensive ablation studies systematically justifying design choices (input refinement effectiveness, GPU acceleration, falsification methods, splitting heuristics)
Strong practical implementation with GPU acceleration (82.8-89.8% speedup) and detailed reproducibility information (hyperparameters, hardware specs, MATLAB/CORA implementation)
Effective presentation with intuitive figures and examples (Example 1 clearly demonstrates refinement mechanism; Figures 1-4 illustrate concepts well)
Rigorous treatment of soundness and computational complexity with formal proofs
weaknesses: Limited novelty: exploiting zonotope-hypercube structure (known since Scott et al., 2016) for input refinement is somewhat incremental; unclear if latent space idea generalizes beyond zonotopes to other set representations
Competitive but not superior results: underperforms on key benchmarks (cora 81.1% vs α-β-CROWN 87.8%; safenlp 89.2% vs 100%), raising questions about practical impact for a top-tier venue

Multiple conservative approximations not thoroughly analyzed: Proposition 2's outer bound is loose for high-dimensional systems; Proposition 3 provides approximate rather than exact bounds; cumulative conservatism effect unclear
Unjustified design choices: fixed refinement iterations (8 per split, 4 per constraint) lack justification; splitting heuristic compared only to local-gradient; missing sensitivity analysis

Limited applicability: approach provides no benefit or hurts performance on low-dimensional benchmarks (acasxu, linearizenn, tllverify-bench); restricted to complete verification with worst-case exponential complexity
Incomplete evaluation: ablation on refinement termination strategy missing; no systematic analysis of performance variance by benchmark; limited insight into failure modes, especially on safenlp
Scalability concerns unaddressed: branch-and-bound exponential worst-case complexity remains; no analysis of when approach will fail to scale with network architecture complexity
